extracted.intended_audience: humor researchers, comedy writers, content analysts, and students of humor studies
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Arthur Asa Berger's 45-technique taxonomy to identify, tag, or analyze humor across media; determine technique(s), dominant category, freshness, and audience fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four basic categories; covers verbal forms of humor. Contains techniques 1–15 (Allusion through Satire). Use when humor is primarily produced through wording, phrasing, or linguistic devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four basic categories; covers ideational or cognitive forms of humor. Contains techniques 16–29 (Absurdity through Unmasking). Use when humor arises from reasoning, expectation, or logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four basic categories; covers humor tied to character, persona, social identity, or existential situations. Contains techniques 30–42 (Before/After through Stereotype).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four basic categories; covers physical, nonverbal, or action-based humor. Contains techniques 43–45 (Chase, Slapstick, Speed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #1, Category: Language. Part of Berger's 45-technique taxonomy; used to tag instances where humor depends on referencing other texts, people, events, or cultural material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #2, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use to tag grandiose, inflated language used for comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #3, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use where humor arises from defining or redefining terms in a humorous way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggeration (verbal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #4, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use for verbal overstatement or hyperbole intended to be funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facetiousness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #5, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use when remarks are made in a flippant or jokingly inappropriate manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insults
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #6, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use to tag humor that depends on disparaging remarks or put-downs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infantilism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #7, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use where childish speech or behavior is the comedic device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #8, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use when meaning is conveyed opposite to literal wording for comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misunderstanding (linguistic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #9, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use for humor based on linguistic miscomprehension, misinterpretation, or ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-literalness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #10, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use when a speaker takes figurative language literally to generate humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puns / Wordplay
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #11, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use for humor driven by multiple meanings, sounds, or playful manipulation of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repartee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #12, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use where quick, witty verbal exchange creates humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ridicule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #13, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use when humor stems from mocking or exposing a target to scorn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarcasm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #14, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use for cutting, often ironic remarks intended to mock or convey contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #15, Category: Language. Part of the taxonomy; use when humor critiques or ridicules social/political institutions or behaviors via irony, exaggeration, or inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #16, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use where events or ideas are wildly illogical or nonsensical to produce humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accident
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #17, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when unintended events or mishaps create comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #18, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when comparing dissimilar things highlights a comic resemblance or incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalogue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #19, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use for lists or enumerations deployed for humorous accumulation or surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coincidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #20, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when unlikely or fortuitous conjunctions are the source of comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #21, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when juxtaposing items yields a comedic effect via contrast or likeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disappointment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #22, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when a gap between expectation and outcome is exploited for humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignorance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #23, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use where lack of knowledge or naiveté produces comedic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #24, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when errors or blunders are the basis of the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #25, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when recurrence or refrain creates humor (through mounting absurdity or pattern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #26, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when expected relationships or roles are inverted to produce humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigidity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #27, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when inflexible thinking or systems generate comedic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme and Variation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #28, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when a central idea is varied repeatedly for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unmasking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #29, Category: Logic. Part of the taxonomy; use when revealing hidden motives, truths, or identities produces humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before/After
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #30, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use to tag contrasts between prior and subsequent states for comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burlesque
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #31, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when low and high styles are mixed for parody or caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caricature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #32, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use where exaggerated features of a person/thing are depicted humorously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eccentricity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #33, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when odd or unconventional traits are the source of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embarrassment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #34, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use where awkward social situations create comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #35, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when revealing private or hidden information produces humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #36, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when bizarre, distorted, or macabre features are employed comically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #37, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when copying mannerisms or speech creates humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #38, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when deliberately portraying someone else for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimicry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #39, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when imitation of sounds, voices, or behaviors produces humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #40, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when an existing work or genre is imitated for comic critique or entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale (gigantism/diminution)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #41, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use when altering size, scope, or magnitude creates comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #42, Category: Identity. Part of the taxonomy; use where generalized traits of groups are invoked for humor (note sensitivity and audience considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chase
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #43, Category: Action. Part of the taxonomy; use for physical pursuit sequences that generate comedic tension and release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slapstick
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #44, Category: Action. Part of the taxonomy; use for physical comedy involving falls, hits, and exaggerated bodily mishaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique #45, Category: Action. Part of the taxonomy; use when rapid pacing or tempo is exploited for humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which of the 45 techniques does the joke employ?
rubrics_metrics.description: Which of the 45 techniques does the joke employ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question from Berger's rubric: identify one or more techniques from the taxonomy that the humor specimen uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is more than one technique combined?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is more than one technique combined?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question from Berger's rubric: assess whether the humorous effect arises from a combination of techniques and, if so, which ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which category dominates (Language/Logic/Identity/Action)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question from Berger's rubric: determine the primary category among the four basic categories that best characterizes the specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the technique used freshly or formulaically?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the technique used freshly or formulaically?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question from Berger's rubric: judge whether the application of the technique feels original and inventive or repetitively formulaic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the technique fit the topic / audience?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the technique fit the topic / audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question from Berger's rubric: assess appropriateness and fit—whether the technique aligns with subject matter and the intended audience's sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy significance and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive and mutually exclusive classification; derived from content analysis of humor in many media; useful for tagging any humor specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-guidance from the page: Berger's taxonomy is presented as comprehensive and mutually exclusive, grounded in content analysis across media, and intended as a practical tagging/analytic tool.
